items.title: Europe's Euclid space telescope finds its first new comet
items.why: The European Space Agency says Euclid, built to map distant galaxies, has found a previously unknown comet, C/2026 S1 (Euclid), about 1.3 billion km from Earth. A University of Helsinki PhD student spotted it in September images; the Minor Planet Center confirmed it on 8 October.
items.matters: It suggests survey telescopes can spot comets far from the Sun, early enough for missions such as ESA's planned Comet Interceptor.

items.title: Yemen officials say Houthi missiles killed at least 50 at army camp
items.why: The Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at a government army training camp in Shabwa province, southern Yemen, on Monday morning, the government says. A Shabwa official told AFP at least 50 people were killed and more than 100 injured. The Houthis say they targeted a 'Saudi-backed' base.
items.matters: US embassies in 12 Middle East countries told Americans on Monday to be highly vigilant, warning the fighting could spread quickly.

items.changed: Updated: index closes about 3.6% lower, below 5,000; exchange to drop about 80 stocks from the index after talks with MSCI
items.title: Indonesian shares slump again after MSCI warns of index downgrade
items.why: Jakarta's main share index closed about 3.6% lower on Monday, below 5,000 points for the first time since 2020, after an 11.6% drop on Friday. After talks with MSCI, the stock exchange said it will remove about 80 stocks with highly concentrated ownership from the index, Nikkei Asia reports.
items.matters: A downgrade could force global index funds to sell Indonesian shares; the rupiah is near its record low against the dollar.

items.title: Elon Musk pledges one SpaceX share to every child in America
items.why: Elon Musk said on X on Monday that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to 'every kid in America'. With more than 70 million under-18s and Friday's closing price of $146, that would be worth over $10 billion. He gave no details.
items.matters: Musk made the pledge in reply to Anthropic's plan to put 5% of its shares into a public benefit fund.

items.title: UN food agency cuts aid to half a million people in Gaza
items.why: The UN World Food Programme said on Monday it will stop monthly food aid for about 500,000 people in Gaza because of a funding shortfall, cutting its caseload from 1.6 million to 1.1 million. It says about two-thirds of Gazans are acutely food insecure.
items.matters: The WFP blames lower donor funding as winter nears; Israel's military aid body, COGAT, says Gaza is well supplied.

items.title: Australian MP Helen Haines critically injured after being hit by car
items.why: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was hit by a four-wheel drive outside her office in Wangaratta, in the Australian state of Victoria, on Monday afternoon. Police say she has critical injuries. A 43-year-old man was detained by bystanders; police say a knife was found in his car.
items.matters: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called it a deliberate act; counter-terrorism police are involved, but police say the motive is not yet known.

items.title: China's economy grows 4.5% in third quarter, slightly beating forecasts
items.why: China's economy grew 4.5% year on year in July–September, official figures showed on Monday, up from 4.3% in the previous quarter and just above the 4.4% economists expected. Retail sales rose 1.1% in September, while investment in property development fell 20.6% in the first nine months.
items.matters: Growth relies on strong exports while shoppers stay cautious, which matters for the many countries that trade with China.

items.title: Rays beat Guardians to move one win from the World Series
items.why: The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 in Cleveland, Ohio, on 18 October to lead the American League Championship Series 3-2. Drew Rasmussen allowed one run in seven innings. Game 6 is on Monday night in St Petersburg, Florida.
items.matters: The series winner plays the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series, which starts on 23 October.

items.title: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro trade insults in first Brazil run-off debate
items.why: Brazil's President Lula and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro met on Sunday night in São Paulo for their first debate before the 25 October run-off. They accused each other of corruption and clashed over security, healthcare and the economy. AFP says two polls this week put Bolsonaro ahead 51% to 49%.
items.matters: The winner will lead Latin America's largest country; a second and final TV debate is scheduled for Friday 23 October.

items.title: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund
items.why: US AI company Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, said on 18 October it will put 5% of its shares into a new fund for public-good projects, subject to shareholder approval. Its board may add 2% for every 50% rise in the company's value.
items.matters: Anthropic says the fund could support people affected by AI-driven job changes; it cannot be used for lobbying or political donations.

items.title: Venezuela's opposition reaffirms exiled Nobel laureate Machado as its leader
items.why: Venezuela's main opposition alliance, meeting in Caracas on Sunday, backed exiled Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado as leader and set out 14 proposals for restoring democracy, including freeing all political prisoners. It called for free elections but set no date; Machado's party wants a vote in 2027.
items.matters: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez has led Venezuela since the US removed Nicolás Maduro in January; separate talks with the opposition exclude her.

items.title: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case as Congo outbreak reaches new province
items.why: Kenya's health ministry confirmed an eighth Ebola case on Sunday: a 49-year-old man who worked as an attendant near the country's first patient and was already in quarantine. Congo says the virus has reached an eighth province, North Ubangi, bordering the Central African Republic.
items.matters: The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment; Congo's latest report counts 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths, Reuters says.

items.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu nine days before Israel's 27 October election
items.why: US President Donald Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, saying that if Israel chose anyone else, America would have to deal with Iran itself. Polls show a tight race; AFP reports neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's is on course for a 61-seat majority.
items.matters: It is Israel's first national election since the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023.

items.title: UN nature summit opens in Armenia with most targets off track
items.why: Nearly 200 countries are meeting in Armenia's capital, Yerevan, for two weeks of UN biodiversity talks, COP17, the first review of a 2022 pact to halt nature loss by 2030. Opening the conference, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said countries are "not yet on track".
items.matters: A UN report says current plans would protect only 26% of land and 12% of oceans by 2030, against a 30% goal.

items.changed: Updated: police say one of the three suspects detained in Kota is a minor and that they planned to flee to Nepal
items.title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff unhurt after gunmen fire at his car
items.why: Gunmen fired at actor Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area, India, on the evening of 18 October, police say. He was unhurt; his driver and another man were injured. Police detained three suspects, one of them a minor, at Kota railway station in Rajasthan on 19 October.
items.matters: Police say the suspects planned to flee to Nepal; an unverified social media post claimed the attack for the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.

items.title: Sergei Loznitsa's Soviet-era documentary Imperium wins top London Film Festival prize
items.why: Imperium, a 175-minute documentary built from footage Italian cameramen shot in the Soviet Union in the early 1970s, won Best Film at the BFI London Film Festival on 18 October. Thailand's 9 Temples to Heaven won the best first feature award.
items.matters: Concrete Land, about a family facing displacement in Jordan, won the festival's documentary prize, the Grierson Award.

items.title: Ethiopians win both Amsterdam Marathon races; Diriba sets women's course record
items.why: Buze Diriba won the women's race in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, on 18 October in 2:16:12, 40 seconds inside the course record, World Athletics says. Fellow Ethiopian Lemi Berhanu won the men's race in 2:03:33, three seconds outside the record.
items.matters: Diriba's run, in wet conditions, moves her to 16th on the world all-time list, World Athletics says.

items.title: China's Ruoning Yin wins LPGA Shanghai, her second straight tour win
items.why: Ruoning Yin won the Buick LPGA Shanghai at Sheshan Golf Club, China, on 18 October at 11 under par, one shot ahead of South Korea's Hye-Jin Choi. It is her seventh LPGA Tour title and her second Shanghai win, after 2024.
items.matters: She had also won her previous LPGA event, the FM Championship near Boston, in August.

items.title: Microsoft pulls out of planned AI data centre near London
items.why: Microsoft has confirmed it withdrew from a deal to rent about 23,000 Nvidia AI chips at a data centre planned by British start-up Nscale in Loughton, northeast of London. Grid officials reportedly told Nscale the site may not get enough power until the 2030s. Nscale says the project continues.
items.matters: The UK government had promoted the site as its largest 'sovereign' AI data centre; grid delays are holding back several such projects.

items.title: Japan set to launch probe to bring back samples from Mars moon
items.why: Japan's space agency JAXA plans to launch its MMX probe on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima at 19:41 UTC on 19 October (04:41 Tuesday, Japan time). It should reach Mars in 2027, collect at least 10 grams from the moon Phobos, and return them in 2031.
items.matters: No mission has yet brought back material from the Mars system; it may show how Mars's two small moons formed.

items.title: Protests in Bogotá after Colombia's government removes works from National Museum
items.why: Riot police used tear gas and a water cannon to break up a protest outside Colombia's National Museum in Bogotá on Saturday, AFP reports. The Culture Ministry had ordered at least 30 pieces removed, on feminism, LGBTQ rights, the 2016 peace deal and assassinated political leaders.
items.matters: The government says the museum must not be 'an instrument of political indoctrination'; six other museums urged it to guarantee museums' autonomy.

items.changed: Updated: Russian strikes on 11 regions overnight cut power to at least 550,000 families, Zelensky says
items.title: Russian strikes cut power to 550,000 Ukrainian homes after drone barrage
items.why: Russia says it downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday; fires hit an oil terminal in St Petersburg. Overnight into Monday, Russia struck energy sites in 11 Ukrainian regions, and President Zelensky says at least 550,000 families lost power. Ukrainian officials say at least four people were killed.
items.matters: Both sides are striking energy sites despite the 'energy ceasefire' US President Donald Trump announced on 11 October.

items.title: Stampede at Durga Puja pavilion in India's Kolkata kills at least 19
items.why: A crowd surged as rain began outside a Durga Puja festival pavilion in Kolkata, eastern India, on Saturday evening. Indian media report at least 19 people died and about 25 were injured. Police have arrested seven people, including organisers.
items.matters: West Bengal's Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari, has ordered an investigation led by a sitting Calcutta High Court judge.

items.title: Rain washes out decider; India and West Indies draw T20 series 2-2
items.why: The fifth and final T20 international in Bengaluru, India, was abandoned on 17 October after India reached 118 for 5 in 7.4 overs of a match cut to nine overs a side. West Indies captain Shai Hope, with two centuries, was player of the series.
items.matters: West Indies have not won a bilateral series in India since 2002-03, ANI reports.

items.title: Manchester City win first seven league games as Haaland reaches milestone
items.why: Manchester City beat Ipswich Town 3-2 in Manchester, England, on 17 October, their seventh Premier League win in seven games. Erling Haaland scored twice, reaching 100 Premier League non-penalty goals in 139 games, the fewest of any player, ESPN says.
items.matters: Arsenal, second, beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 on Sunday and are three points behind City.

items.changed: Updated: Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, arrived in Tehran on Monday for talks on preventing renewed war
items.title: Russia's Lavrov in Tehran for talks as Hormuz ship attacks continue
items.why: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov arrived in Tehran on Monday, his first visit since the war began, saying Moscow wants to prevent a return to large-scale war. UKMTO says a tug was hit off the UAE; Iran says Hormuz would reopen within six days if the US lifts its blockade.
items.matters: Al Jazeera reports more ships attacked this month than in any month since the Iran war began in February.

items.changed: Updated: the prime minister ordered local curfews on Monday and did not rule out a state of emergency
items.title: France orders local curfews after weekend of riots and looting
items.why: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu asked prefects on Monday to impose partial, local curfews in some cities after cost-of-living protests turned into riots and looting. He said a state of emergency was possible 'if necessary'. The interior ministry says about 2,400 were arrested on Saturday; Macron refused his interior minister's resignation.
items.matters: Macron admits 'failures in anticipation and intelligence'; the unrest is seen as a test of the mood before the 2027 election.

items.changed: Updated: Brent eases about 2% after Trump waives Russia sanctions
items.title: Oil eases from five-month high after US waives Russia sanctions
items.why: Brent crude fell about 2% to near $108 a barrel on Monday 19 October, after touching $110 on Friday. Traders expect more Russian fuel exports after President Trump waived key US sanctions and tariffs on Russia. Attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz continue to cut Gulf supplies.
items.matters: Prices remain well above pre-war levels, keeping pressure on fuel, transport and food costs.

items.changed: Updated: four more deaths; the toll is now 352, with 107 in October so far
items.title: Bangladesh dengue deaths reach 352 this year as cases pass 114,000
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate reported four more dengue deaths in the 24 hours to Monday morning, bringing this year's toll to 352, with 114,251 cases. October has seen 107 deaths so far, after 148 in September, the deadliest month this year.
items.matters: Dengue, spread by mosquitoes, has no specific treatment; Bangladesh's government has ordered neighbourhood awareness campaigns to curb it.

items.changed: Updated: fire hotspots in Indonesia almost quadrupled on Sunday, and Singapore has served notices on three more firms, 10 in all
items.title: Indonesia's fires push South-East Asia's haze alert to highest level
items.why: Smoke from Indonesia's worst forest fires in a decade keeps southern South-East Asia under the regional haze monitor's highest alert. Indonesia's forestry ministry says fire hotspots rose to 1,104 on Sunday from 270 a day earlier, most in Kalimantan, on Borneo.
items.matters: Haze has disrupted 2,458 Indonesian flights since August; Singapore has ordered 10 Indonesian firms it links to the fires to act.

items.changed: Updated: Champi is a super typhoon again east of the Philippines and is heading for waters off northern Luzon and Taiwan
items.title: Champi regains super typhoon strength, heading for waters off Luzon and Taiwan
items.why: After passing just south of Guam on Sunday, Champi regained super typhoon strength on Monday about 1,500 km east of Luzon, with winds of 185 km/h, the Philippine weather agency PAGASA says. It should enter Philippine waters on Tuesday, where it will be called Rosal.
items.matters: Taiwan's weather agency expects Champi to turn north before reaching the island but bring heavy rain on Friday and Saturday.
